$comment: Transcribed by hand from the SIA chart set AD 2 LFGA (AIP France, chart dated 2026-08-06): the text pages checked against the images of the pages.
Only what the chart states is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text; the reporting points, rules and notes were added by hand.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.
No reporting points, circuit height or circuit side are printed on this chart, so none is recorded.

A "fr" object holds the French column of the same chart, copied as printed and never translated: a French note sits at the index of its English twin and is left empty when the twin could not be paired with certainty; the French of the procedures and of the points' purposes is not recorded.

The French of "circuit", "withAts" and "withoutAts" is in "fr": same tree as the English, text values only, written by hand from the French column of the chart where it was read, and translated from the English text otherwise; point and runway identifiers are repeated unchanged.
name: Colmar - Houssen

service.atsHours: TWR: November to March, Monday to Friday 0630 to 1900, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays 0730 to sunset + 30 min (1830 at most); April to October, Monday to Friday 0630 to 2000, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays 0730 to sunset + 30 min (1730 at most) (UTC in winter, local time minus 1 h in summer)
service.outsideAtsHours: AFIS 119.000 on PPR 18 HR to the aerodrome operator, available only between sunset + 30 min and sunrise - 30 min; otherwise air-air 119.000, French only

circuit.lowHeight: low-height traffic circuits on PPR with COLMAR TWR: west circuits minimum 300 ft AAL, east circuits minimum 500 ft AAL

notes: Aerodrome reserved for radio-equipped aircraft. Prohibited to PUL. ULM activity: multi-axis ULM only. IFR operations at both QFU.

Simultaneous use of both runways is prohibited. The unpaved runway is reserved (except for safety reasons) for gliders, tow planes and based aircraft of the CICVVA fleet; outside gliding activity it is usable only by aircraft authorised by the aerodrome operator.

Take-off from an intermediate part of runway 01/19 is prohibited (not applicable to based aircraft whose reference take-off distance is under 800 m for a runway 19 take-off from the intersection with taxiway EN). TORA available from the taxiway EN intersection: 1350 m.
Heavy turbulence with a west wind abeam the hangars west of the aerodrome.

Obstacles in the strip: runway 19, bushes and vines in the runway strip and a frangible fence, lit by day and night, in the cleared strip 45 m north of the threshold 19; runway 01, a section of street along the west of the aerodrome lies in the runway strip.
Heavy helicopter activity at the Pasteur hospital, 2 NM south of the runway, within the Colmar aerodrome traffic.
IFR training is prohibited outside ATS hours; night training is prohibited outside ATS hours.
The surroundings are very noise-sensitive: noise abatement measures are detailed in the environment charter on the aerodrome operator website.

The north-east parking is reserved for based aircraft; radio contact with COLMAR TWR is mandatory at points E1, E2 and E3. Taxiing prohibited except on runways and taxiways; taxiway E3 is reserved for aircraft parked at hangars H14-H15; taxiways E4/E5 are reserved for gliders.
By night and with RVR below 800 m, aircraft whose take-off reference distance is 1200 m or more must use taxiway EC (arrivals and departures).
Non-8.33 kHz aircraft contact the ATS on the COLMAR Tower frequency, on departure and, unless otherwise instructed, on arrival.
Radio failure: apply the national regulation and, if possible, use a mobile phone to contact the TWR.

Pilot-controlled lighting and STAP are available on PPR to the aerodrome operator by e-mail before 1500: 3 clicks within 5 seconds, information and low-intensity lighting; 5 clicks within 5 seconds, information and high-intensity lighting; 7 clicks within 5 seconds, lights off.
Aerobatics out of the aerodrome no. 6160 and paradropping no. 221: see AIP ENR 5.5.
Panne de radiocommunication Appliquer la règlementation nationale et si possible, utiliser le téléphone portable pour contacter la TWR.
